milestones.title: Pipeline Kernel
success_criteria: Default pipeline can be constructed from registered stage factories.
Tests prove stage order and stop behavior.

milestones.title: Pipeline Policy Stages
success_criteria: Non-eligible events stop before process/provider stages.
Policy stages are configured through PipelineContext ports.

milestones.title: Process Stage
success_criteria: Plugin commands can suppress provider fallback.
Plugin-generated provider requests flow into provider execution.

milestones.title: Respond And Result Decoration
success_criteria: Streaming and non-streaming response paths are independently testable.

milestones.title: Context Session And Memory
success_criteria: Pipeline stages read session context through traits, not concrete storage.
Tests prove per-session provider selection and context injection.

milestones.title: Runtime Assembly And Reload
success_criteria: Runtime restart rebuilds pipeline from config.
Reload tests prove old background tasks are stopped.

milestones.title: Platform Provider And Dashboard Breadth
success_criteria: Dashboard never reaches into EventBus/Pipeline internals.

key_decisions: Use Maestro workflow files as the source of progress management.
Treat the current branch as greenfield and do not reuse prior deleted implementation files.
Learn AstrBot's architecture and product philosophy, but design Rust boundaries independently.
First implementation validates Platform -> EventBus -> Pipeline -> Provider -> Respond with mocks.
OpenAI-compatible Provider is implemented behind ChatProvider with local HTTP mock coverage.
ProviderRegistry and ProviderManager now mirror AstrBot's provider_cls_map/inst_map/default_provider_id pattern with typed Rust config.
Minimal PluginRegistry and PluginStage now mirror AstrBot Star handler metadata/filter/priority concepts.
AstrbotRuntime now centralizes lifecycle assembly: config -> provider manager -> plugin registry -> pipeline scheduler -> event bus/platform.
Runtime keeps provider optional at pipeline assembly time so command plugins can respond without a configured chat provider.
PlatformRegistry and PlatformManager now mirror AstrBot's platform_cls_map plus load_platform pattern with typed Rust platform config.
AstrbotRuntime constructs platforms through PlatformManager instead of directly constructing MockPlatform.
RuntimeHandle now owns background EventBus and platform adapter task handles, mirroring AstrBotCoreLifecycle start/stop task ownership.
RuntimeConfig now creates missing config files and writes back missing default runtime keys after successful parsing.
RuntimeHandle::restart now rebuilds a fresh runtime from config after stopping the old one.
astrbot-cli now exposes thin init/run/smoke commands while delegating lifecycle work to astrbot-runtime.
ConsolePlatform is the first non-mock adapter and enters runtime only through PlatformRegistry and PlatformManager.
WebChatPlatform now provides a dashboard-ready external input boundary that submits text into EventBus without coupling HTTP to runtime.
astrbot-web provides a thin HTTP boundary that maps requests to WebChatPlatform without touching pipeline/runtime internals.
astrbot-cli run can now launch WebChat HTTP as a sibling transport service using the runtime-created WebChatPlatform and config-driven host/port.
WebChat HTTP readback now uses WebChatPlatform conversation history instead of reaching into EventBus/Pipeline internals.
OpenAI-compatible provider can now opt into SSE-style streaming and collect chunks into the final ChatResponse without changing the pipeline contract.
OpenAI-compatible provider now preserves text-only payloads while switching to OpenAI content parts when ChatRequest includes image URLs.
ProviderStage now forwards MessageChain image URLs into ChatRequest, including image-only events.
WebChat submit now accepts text plus image URLs behind the platform boundary, keeping HTTP transport thin and allowing image-only events.
WebChat HTTP submit now accepts typed plain/image message parts and submits the normalized MessageChain through WebChatPlatform::submit_chain.
WebChat history readback now serializes recorded MessageChain replies as text, image URLs, and typed plain/image message parts.
Core MessageComponent and WebChat typed parts now preserve record, video, and file media while ProviderStage remains limited to text and image URLs.
WebChat reply parts now round-trip as lightweight Reply components, with reply-only messages treated as empty content.
Migration direction is now pipeline-first: finish the lower-level stage registry/order/lifecycle and policy stages before expanding more upper-layer platform/dashboard breadth.
PipelineStageRegistry now owns built-in plugin/provider/respond stage factories and deterministic order; runtime default pipeline construction goes through the registry.
PipelineStage now has an initialize hook and PipelineScheduler initializes stages in deterministic order before runtime starts event processing.
DefaultPipelineBuilder now owns built-in registry construction, scheduler creation, and initialization; M1 pipeline kernel is complete and current focus moves to M2 policy stages.

WakeCheckStage now implements the first policy stage: direct messages wake by default, group messages require wake prefix or bot addressing, and non-eligible events stop before plugin/provider/respond.
WhitelistCheckStage, SessionStatusCheckStage, and RateLimitStage now sit behind PipelineContext policy config/ports and run before plugin/provider/respond.
ContentSafetyCheckStage completes M2 policy stages with a ContentSafetyStrategy trait and keyword strategy before plugin/provider/respond.
Default pipeline now uses ProcessStage as the unified plugin/provider facade: wake -> whitelist -> session_status -> rate_limit -> content_safety -> process -> respond.
ProviderRequest now lives at the MessageEvent boundary so plugins can generate typed LLM requests that ProcessStage converts into ChatRequest.
ProviderFallbackConfig now controls LLM fallback enablement, implicit wake gating, and generic provider-error replies; M3 Process Stage is complete.
ResultDecorateStage now sits between process and respond and owns the first result transform: configurable reply prefix.

RespondStage now delegates result-chain cleanup to MessageChain validators: empty plain/media components are removed, reply/mention-only chains are skipped, and stopped empty results still stop the pipeline.

MessageStream and MessageSink::send_streaming now define the streaming response boundary; RespondStage routes streaming results separately, marks StreamingFinish, and suppresses duplicate post-stream sends. M4 Respond And Result Decoration is complete.
SessionContextPort now lets ProviderStage/ProcessStage inject typed ProviderContextMessage history into ProviderRequest without coupling pipeline to concrete conversation storage.
ProviderPreferencePort now resolves session-scoped chat provider IDs before ChatRequest conversion, while ProviderManager implements ChatProvider and routes requests by provider_id.

QuoteContextPolicy now enriches valid ProviderRequest flows with Reply.selected_text as extra user content while reply-only messages still do not trigger provider fallback. M5 Context Session And Memory is complete.
Runtime now owns an InMemoryProviderPreferencePort and injects it into the default PipelineContext, proving M5 provider preference works through the M6 runtime assembly path.
RuntimeStatePolicyConfig now makes restart state behavior explicit: provider preference is preserved by default and can be discarded by config.

ChatProvider, PlatformAdapter, and PluginHandler now expose default terminate hooks; RuntimeHandle::stop stops tasks and then terminates plugin, provider, and platform managers. M6 Runtime Assembly And Reload is complete.

OneBotPlatform is the first real platform-shaped adapter in M7: it enters only through PlatformRegistry/PlatformManager, maps private/group text into unified MessageEvent, preserves direct/group session kind, and defers real OneBot network transport.

ProviderRegistry now mirrors AstrBot's OpenAI-compatible provider subclass family with registry aliases for zhipu, groq, xai, aihubmix, and openrouter; M7-T2 remains in progress for non-OpenAI protocols and provider capability split.

AnthropicProvider is the first native non-OpenAI chat provider in M7-T2: ProviderRegistry owns construction, runtime config maps anthropic_chat_completion, and unsupported streaming/remote image conversion fail explicitly until stream/media boundaries are designed.

GeminiProvider adds AstrBot-compatible googlegenai_chat_completion as a native generateContent provider: ProviderRegistry owns construction, runtime config maps typed settings, and unsupported streaming/remote image conversion fail explicitly until stream/media/tool capability boundaries are designed.

ProviderRegistry now carries ProviderCapability metadata inspired by AstrBot ProviderType, so future STT/TTS/Embedding/Rerank adapters can be registered without being misused as ChatProvider factories.

EmbeddingProvider boundary now mirrors AstrBot EmbeddingProvider/get_dim and manager capability bucket, but remains provider-crate-only with mock implementation until concrete OpenAI/Gemini embedding HTTP providers are added.

OpenAiEmbeddingProvider adds AstrBot-compatible openai_embedding behind the EmbeddingProvider trait and ProviderRegistry, preserving AstrBot's /embeddings payload shape, default text-embedding-3-small model, 1024 dimensions, and /v1 base URL normalization without wiring runtime or pipeline yet.

GeminiEmbeddingProvider adds AstrBot-compatible gemini_embedding behind the EmbeddingProvider trait and ProviderRegistry, mapping Google REST embedContent/batchEmbedContents and keeping non-chat runtime/pipeline wiring deferred.

RerankProvider boundary now mirrors AstrBot RerankProvider/RerankResult and manager capability bucket, but remains provider-crate-only with mock implementation until concrete VLLM/Xinference/Bailian rerank adapters are added.

VllmRerankProvider adds AstrBot-compatible vllm_rerank behind the RerankProvider trait and ProviderRegistry, preserving AstrBot's /v1/rerank payload shape and bearer auth while keeping runtime/pipeline wiring deferred.

BailianRerankProvider adds AstrBot-compatible bailian_rerank behind the RerankProvider trait and ProviderRegistry, preserving DashScope text-rerank payload shape, required bearer auth, qwen3-rerank instruct handling, and API-code error parsing while keeping runtime/pipeline wiring deferred.

SpeechToTextProvider and TextToSpeechProvider boundaries now mirror AstrBot STTProvider/TTSProvider capability buckets with typed request/response traits, mock providers, registry factories, manager routing, and terminate hooks while keeping concrete voice providers and runtime wiring deferred.

XinferenceRerankProvider adds AstrBot-compatible xinference_rerank behind the RerankProvider trait and ProviderRegistry, preserving lazy model UID resolution, optional model launch, rerank result parsing, and keeping runtime/pipeline wiring deferred.

OpenAiTextToSpeechProvider adds AstrBot-compatible openai_tts_api behind the TextToSpeechProvider trait and ProviderRegistry, preserving OpenAI-compatible audio speech payloads, bearer auth, generated audio file output, and keeping runtime/pipeline wiring deferred.

OpenAiSpeechToTextProvider adds AstrBot-compatible openai_whisper_api behind the SpeechToTextProvider trait and ProviderRegistry, preserving OpenAI-compatible audio transcription multipart requests, local/HTTP audio input, auth-isolated audio downloads, and keeping SILK/AMR/Tencent conversion plus runtime/pipeline wiring deferred.

XinferenceSpeechToTextProvider adds AstrBot-compatible xinference_stt behind the SpeechToTextProvider trait and ProviderRegistry, preserving lazy audio model UID resolution, optional model launch, OpenAI-compatible transcription multipart requests, auth-isolated audio downloads, and explicit media conversion deferral.

AudioInputLoader and AudioMediaConverter now define the shared STT audio media conversion boundary, centralizing local/HTTP audio loading, SILK/AMR/Tencent detection, auth-isolated downloads, and explicit unsupported conversion behavior outside concrete STT providers.

GeminiTextToSpeechProvider adds AstrBot-compatible gemini_tts behind the TextToSpeechProvider trait and ProviderRegistry, preserving Gemini generateContent audio response shape, voice config, inline base64 PCM decoding, 24 kHz mono 16-bit WAV output, and keeping runtime/pipeline/dashboard wiring deferred.
Runtime now maps non-chat provider config arrays into ProviderManager capability buckets for STT, TTS, Embedding, and Rerank while keeping PipelineContext chat-only.

VolcengineTextToSpeechProvider adds AstrBot-compatible volcengine_tts behind the TextToSpeechProvider trait and ProviderRegistry, preserving Volcengine payload/header/base64 MP3 behavior while keeping adapter-only fields in provider_options.

MiniMaxTextToSpeechProvider adds AstrBot-compatible minimax_tts_api behind the TextToSpeechProvider trait and ProviderRegistry, preserving streaming SSE hex MP3 collection while keeping MiniMax-only fields in provider_options.
GsviTextToSpeechProvider adds AstrBot-compatible gsvi_tts_api behind the TextToSpeechProvider trait and ProviderRegistry, preserving the thin GET /tts WAV response boundary.

astrbot-platform is now split into core, built, registry, manager, and adapters modules; future WeChat, QQ, OneBot transport, and other platform implementations should live under adapters while runtime/dashboard continue to enter through PlatformRegistry and PlatformManager.
deferred: Plugin lifecycle loading and hot reload
WebChat media upload to image URL conversion, true streaming propagation, and tool-call orchestration for OpenAI-compatible Provider

Provider parity beyond OpenAI-compatible aliases, Anthropic, Gemini chat, capability metadata, embedding providers, rerank boundary, VLLM rerank, Bailian rerank, Xinference Rerank, STT/TTS boundaries, OpenAI TTS, Gemini TTS, Volcengine TTS, MiniMax TTS, GSVI TTS, OpenAI Whisper STT, Xinference STT, shared audio media conversion boundary, and generic non-chat runtime config: remaining voice/provider adapters, concrete media conversion adapter, and provider-specific runtime schemas
Additional real platform adapters and full OneBot reverse WebSocket/HTTP transport behind PlatformRegistry
Runtime config schema/version policy and unknown-key strategy
Richer CLI parsing once command surface grows
Dashboard UI mounting and management APIs for WebChatPlatform
Persistent WebChat conversation storage and SSE/WebSocket response streaming
HTTP auth/session management for WebChat routes
Quote/reply history lookup, quoted image/file extraction, and sender nickname formatting
Persistent provider preference storage and stale provider ID cleanup

transition_history.reason: M3 ProcessStage success criteria completed: plugin suppression, plugin-generated ProviderRequest flow, and provider fallback disable policy.
M4 success criteria completed: empty result chains are skipped and streaming/non-streaming response paths are independently testable.
M5 success criteria completed: session context, provider preference, and quote context all flow through PipelineContext traits without concrete storage coupling.
M6 success criteria completed: runtime default assembly carries M1-M5 contracts, restart state policy is explicit, and manager termination hooks are wired.
